behaviors.depth: Motion staged in depth: perspective, layered parallax, or a genuine 3D scene. The scene design record states whether depth is 2.5D layered composition or genuine 3D.
behaviors.dissolve: A controlled opacity crossfade between two states or shots, computed from the frame clock. Permitted only under the emotional_dissolve intent.
behaviors.eased: Non-linear interpolation with an easing curve (cubic-bezier or a named ease function) that does not overshoot the target value.
behaviors.hard_cut: An instantaneous change of state or framing at a frame boundary, with no interpolation.
behaviors.hold: A deliberate still interval. The frame is composed and readable; stillness is the chosen behavior, not a missing animation.
behaviors.linear: Constant-rate interpolation between two states. The default for data marks and measured change.
behaviors.mask: A reveal or concealment through a mask or clip path, so the subject itself enters or changes.
behaviors.spring: Spring physics toward a target, using the named presets in references/motion-grammar.md (weighty, panel, snap, drift). Some presets overshoot; see the data_marks rule.

coherence.rule: One intent per scene, at most 3 declared behaviors in one scene, and at most 5 distinct behaviors across a whole sequence. A sequence that uses every behavior at once has no vocabulary; it has noise. The linter enforces the two per-scene numbers; the sequence number is review doctrine for the planner and the orchestrator.

data_marks.rule: When a scene animates data marks (chart bars, line points, counters, any element whose position or size encodes a value), spring is forbidden on the marks themselves because an overshooting spring temporarily states a value the data does not contain. Containers, labels, and non-data subjects may spring. This mirrors the MG-015 chart contracts.

detection.depth: perspective and rotateX / rotateY / rotate3d transforms
detection.eased: cubic-bezier( and easeIn / easeOut / easeInOut function calls
detection.note: How scripts/lint-grammar.py recognizes behaviors in legacy scene source. Detected-but-undeclared behavior is a violation; declared behavior is always checked against the declared intent's permitted set.
detection.spring: spring( helper calls, and the preset names weighty, snap, drift (panel is recognized through the spring helper call form)

continuous_data_change.label: Continuous data change
continuous_data_change.notes: Spring is not permitted for this intent: a spring that overshoots a data mark misstates the value (MG-015). A container around the chart may spring; the marks themselves interpolate on the data scale and stop at the true value.
continuous_data_change.purpose: A chart, counter, or measured quantity develops over time and the viewer reads the values as they change.

decisive_reveal.label: Decisive reveal
decisive_reveal.notes: The reveal is the event; it ends in a hold long enough to read. Overshooting spring forms are for physical, playful subjects, never for essential text or data marks.
decisive_reveal.purpose: A subject, claim, or product detail lands once, clearly, and stays readable.

emotional_dissolve.label: Emotional dissolve
emotional_dissolve.notes: This is the only intent whose permitted set includes dissolve. A dissolve is a chosen emotional beat, never the default join between every pair of shots.
emotional_dissolve.purpose: One shot or state gives way to another for feeling: a memory, a transition in time, a softening between testimonial beats.

spatial_travel.label: Spatial travel
spatial_travel.notes: Depth belongs to this intent when the staging is genuinely spatial. A camera move alone does not prove a mechanism; the traveling subject must carry the meaning.
spatial_travel.purpose: A subject moves through a space or layout, and the movement itself explains a relationship, a journey, or a mechanism.

stable_explanation.label: Stable explanation
stable_explanation.notes: Stillness is the point. A slow eased push is allowed; nothing in this intent competes with the words. CTA frames use this intent so the call to action gets its full reading time.
stable_explanation.purpose: A presenter, diagram, or composed frame explains while staying essentially still, so reading is never interrupted by motion.
